title: State-Dependent Capacity
definition: The principle that what a person can perceive, think, feel, and do varies with their current regulatory state.
summary: State-dependent capacity explains why the same person can be warm and cold, insightful and rigid, empathic and dismissive — depending on where their nervous system is positioned. It is neurobiological reality.

content.title: What It Is
content.content: State-dependent capacity is the principle that cognitive, emotional, and relational abilities are not fixed traits but vary with nervous system state. In Connection: broad perceptual field, full empathy access, cognitive flexibility, capacity for repair. In Protection: narrow focus, reduced empathy, rigid thinking, repair feels threatening. In Control/Domination: strategic calculation replaces genuine empathy, power becomes the only felt source of safety.

content.title: How TEG-Blue Maps It
content.content: TEG-Blue uses state-dependent capacity to map empathy access, cognitive flexibility, and relational capacity as functions of regulatory state. The inability to understand another person may not be unwillingness — it may be that the current state has literally reduced the neurobiological capacity to do so. Intervention follows: restore safety first, then expect capacity. This reframes treatment from demanding change to providing conditions for change.

content.title: Research Basis
content.content: Grounded in Siegel's window of tolerance model, Fredrickson's broaden-and-build theory, and polyvagal theory's hierarchy of autonomic states. Each tradition demonstrates that regulatory state constrains available cognitive and emotional resources. TEG-Blue synthesizes these into a unified principle applicable across the Four-Mode Gradient.
